module_summary: dash_devices.c is the dashboard's device model: it builds the DashDevice rows (memory cards, USB, MMCE, MX4SIO, iLink, HDD/ATA, PC CARD CF, disc, UDPFS, SMB/NFS, host, PSX flash/DVR, VMC) from cached driver/probe state, probes a device on explicit open through the init.c lazy loaders (startSync on the UI thread behind a loading overlay), runs boot auto-start of the configured device families, tracks hotplug for connect/disconnect sounds and decides whether a cached application path is usable. dash_files.c is the Devices section: a list mode (File Browser root, last folder, MISC, PathPad bookmarks) and a card grid of the devices, switched with SELECT via dashCfg.files_mode. dash_editor.c is the native multi-document Text Editor (gap-less buffer with a line table, EOL detection/restore, docked keyboard, USB keyboard, file IO on the worker) plus an in-place Hex Editor that reuses the same worker IO job and layout. dash_exploit.c adapts the classic memory card exploit installer (main_exploit_installer.c) to dashboard widgets through the ExploitInstallerUi callback table; the classic path (main_actions.c:803) still uses it with the table unset.

reusable_helpers.name: probeRoot
reusable_helpers.what: polls fileXioDopen on a device root every 100 ms up to a deadline while keeping the loading overlay animated

reusable_helpers.name: dashDevicePathReady
reusable_helpers.what: side-effect-free test whether the storage behind a path (mc, usb/mass, vmc, cdfs, rom, CF, other stacks) is currently usable

reusable_helpers.name: dashBootDeviceBit
reusable_helpers.what: maps the boot directory prefix to its DASH_DEVA_* device-family bit

reusable_helpers.name: docSetText
reusable_helpers.what: detects CRLF/LF/CR line endings of a buffer and normalises it to LF in place

reusable_helpers.name: docFileBytes
reusable_helpers.what: converts an LF text buffer back to CRLF, LF or CR bytes for saving

reusable_helpers.name: edIoRun
reusable_helpers.what: worker job that reads a whole file (chunked, size-capped) or writes/overwrites it through genOpen/genRead/genWrite

reusable_helpers.name: hexParse
reusable_helpers.what: parses a hex number with optional 0x prefix

reusable_helpers.name: deviceDisplayMount
reusable_helpers.what: turns a usbN: device mount into its user-facing massN:/ label

findings.title: dash_files.c list mode keeps a dead FE_DEVICE path and an unused 4.5 KB fdevs[] array
findings.problem: filesRebuild never adds an FE_DEVICE entry (it only sets nfdevs = 0 at line 212, 'Devices are the alternate mode'), so fdevs[] is never filled and every FE_DEVICE branch in filesActivate, the row dot and the detail panel is unreachable. The 1-second periodic filesRebuild in filesUpdate (comment: 'device states change') and the 'Refresh devices' menu item only re-read LastDir/PathPad, which already rebuild on enter and after every activation.
findings.fix: Delete FE_DEVICE, fdevs, nfdevs and the three FE_DEVICE branches (keep the else body of the detail panel), delete the timer part of filesUpdate (keep the fsel_anim line) and the 'Refresh devices' menu item.
findings.benefit: ~30 lines; 4512 bytes of .bss RAM (INFERRED: sizeof(DashDevice) = 4+4+32+24+24+48+48+4 = 188 bytes x DASH_MAX_DEVICES 24); one needless list rebuild per second removed
findings.evidence: Grep FE_DEVICE|nfdevs|fdevs over src/Launchstation: only dash_files.c:164,181,182,212,288-290,374-375,392-393; no fAdd(FE_DEVICE, ...) anywhere. DashDevice struct at include/dash_internal.h:782-792, DASH_MAX_DEVICES 24 at :794. fdevs is referenced by code so it is kept in .bss (no -fdata-sections, BUILD-EVIDENCE.md:107).

findings.title: dashDevicesStart is synchronous but callers use a callback plus deferred pend/pick state to get its result
findings.problem: dashDevicesStart runs startSync/probeMount on the UI thread and calls cb before it returns (dash_devices.c:765-773); `user` is NULL at every call site and both callbacks (pendProbeDone, pickStartDone) ignore mount and user and only latch ok. dash_files.c then keeps a pend struct, an 'Another device is still starting' guard, a per-frame dashFilesPoll from dash_main.c and a section-changed branch, although the result is already known when the call returns; dash_widgets.c does the same with pk.start_done/start_ok.
findings.fix: Drop DashProbeDone, cb and user; return the probe result directly (keep -1 for backed out and 1 for refused, e.g. return 2/0 for usable/not found or move refused to -2). Handle the result inline in startDevice and in the picker, and delete pend, pendProbeDone, dashFilesPoll (and its call and prototype), pickStartDone and the start_done/start_ok fields. Update tests/test_udpfs_retry.py:22 and test_device_input.py, which assert on the old call text.
findings.benefit: ~40 lines across dash_devices.c, dash_files.c, dash_widgets.c, dash_main.c, dash_internal.h (INFERRED from cited ranges); one function call per frame removed
findings.evidence: Callers (grep dashDevicesStart): dash_files.c:135 (pendProbeDone, NULL), dash_widgets.c:1209 (pickStartDone, NULL), dash_browser.c:694 (NULL, NULL). Read pendProbeDone dash_files.c:77-83 and pickStartDone dash_widgets.c:960-966: both (void)mount/(void)user. dashFilesPoll only called at dash_main.c:1450, same loop iteration as the input that started the device. INFERRED: dashWorkerAwaitAll/loading overlay cannot change the current section, so the section-mismatch branch dash_files.c:92-96 is unreachable.

findings.title: Feature #ifdefs in dash_devices.c/dash_files.c test macros every build always defines
findings.problem: MMCE, MX4SIO, ILINK, XFROM, DVRP, EXFAT, UDPFS, SMB and ETH are unconditionally defined for the only EE target (ps2.yaml:618-629), and the DS34 variant only adds DS34 (scripts/configure_ds34.py:36), so 82 directive lines in dash_devices.c and 4 in dash_files.c guard code that is always compiled. Unlike the code elsewhere, dashBootDeviceBit (lines 909-916) already uses ata/mmce/mx4sio/ilink without guards, so the files are not even consistent.
findings.fix: Delete the #ifdef/#endif lines for these macros in both files (keep the guarded code). If the owner wants the macros gone repo-wide, do it in one pass with the other dash_* files. Host tests that paste these functions (tests/test_device_input.py:210-213 defines only MMCE, MX4SIO, EXFAT, UDPFS) need the extra stubs for SMB/ILINK paths.
findings.benefit: 86 preprocessor lines removed (MEASURED: Grep count of ^#(if|ifdef|ifndef|else|endif) = 82 in dash_devices.c, 4 in dash_files.c); no ELF change
findings.evidence: Read ps2.yaml:614-630 (defines list) and scripts/configure_ds34.py:34-39 (only adds DS34, swaps pad.c). No other build file builds these sources. Grep count of directives in the four unit files: dash_devices.c 82, dash_files.c 4, dash_editor.c 0, dash_exploit.c 0. Grep of tests for '#define MMCE' etc: test_device_input.py:210-213 defines a subset.

findings.title: autoStartNeeded repeats dashDevicesAutoProbe's per-family mask/loaded tests
findings.problem: autoStartNeeded and the pass body of dashDevicesAutoProbe write the same six '(mask & DASH_DEVA_X) && !isPathDeviceStackLoaded("x:")' tests for HDD, ATA, MMCE, MX4SIO, iLink and UDPFS, one returning a boolean and the other calling probeMount on the same mount strings; a new family must be added in both places.
findings.fix: Put the six {bit, mount} pairs in one static const table and loop over it in both functions (USB stays a separate last step in AutoProbe and a separate test in autoStartNeeded).
findings.justification: The table is data that replaces about 30 lines of repeated conditions with two short loops; it removes code and keeps the two lists from drifting.
findings.benefit: ~20 lines (INFERRED: 22 + 22 condition lines become a 7-line table and two ~6-line loops); a few hundred bytes of .text at most (INFERRED)
findings.evidence: Read dash_devices.c:698-720 and 856-890 side by side: identical bit/mount pairs hdd0:, ata0:, mmce0:, mx4sio:, ilink:, udpfs:. Both are only used inside dash_devices.c (autoStartNeeded static; dashDevicesAutoProbe called at :796 and from tests). tests/test_device_autostart_safe_mode.py:37-41 asserts 'const int mask = safeAutoStartMask();' in both, which the change keeps.

findings.title: safeAutoStartMask re-checks MMCE/MX4SIO exclusivity already enforced on load and on toggle
findings.problem: dashCfg.dev_auto is only written in dash_store.c (default 0, parse at :358 followed by the same MMCE/MX4SIO normalisation at :448-454) and in dash_settings.c:1755-1764, which clears the other bit or refuses the toggle; whole-struct restores (dash_settings.c:2573, 2758) copy already-normalised snapshots. The 'defense in depth' copy in safeAutoStartMask can never see both bits set.
findings.fix: Delete lines 685-694 of dash_devices.c and keep only the iLink masking in safeAutoStartMask.
findings.evidence: Grep 'dev_auto\s*(\||&|\^)?=' over src: dash_settings.c:1756,1758,1762,1764; dash_store.c:259,358,451,453. Grep 'dashCfg\s*=[^=]': dash_settings.c:2573 (snap_dash), 2758 (saved). Read dash_store.c:435-455 and dash_settings.c:1740-1767. Tests asserting the store/settings copies: test_device_autostart_safe_mode.py:31-32,49-50; none asserts the dash_devices.c copy.

findings.title: dash_devices.c exports with no outside user: dashMcPresent (test-only), dashDiscStatus, dashDevicesAutoProbe
findings.problem: dashMcPresent has no production caller (only tests/test_device_input.py:394-395); dashDiscStatus is only called at dash_devices.c:443 and dashDevicesAutoProbe only at dash_devices.c:796, yet both are exported through dash_internal.h.
findings.fix: Delete dashMcPresent and its prototype (drop the two test asserts); make dashDiscStatus and dashDevicesAutoProbe static and delete their prototypes.
findings.benefit: ~7 lines; no ELF change (dashMcPresent is already discarded by -ffunction-sections + --gc-sections, BUILD-EVIDENCE.md:107-108)
findings.evidence: Grep dashMcPresent|dashDiscStatus|dashDevicesAutoProbe over src/Launchstation (c, h, py, md): dashMcPresent dash_devices.c:187, dash_internal.h:809, tests/test_device_input.py:394-395; dashDiscStatus dash_devices.c:254,443, dash_internal.h:808; dashDevicesAutoProbe dash_devices.c:796,856, dash_internal.h:797, tests (own static stubs in test_startup_status.py:61, test_device_input.py:310), docs/plans only.

findings.title: Small copy-paste in dash_devices.c: dashDevicesInit repeats ResetBaseline; PC CARD CF row written as 8 add() calls
findings.problem: dashDevicesInit (dash_main.c:1283) repeats the three baseline assignments of dashDevicesResetBaseline (dash_main.c:362). The PC CARD CF block calls add() eight times with the same icon, name, 'cf0:' and 'cf0:/', differing only in state and status text.
findings.fix: Have dashDevicesInit call dashDevicesResetBaseline. In the CF block pick state and status in the if/else chain and make one add() call afterwards (then fill the capacity detail when READY).
findings.benefit: ~10 lines (INFERRED: 3 in Init, ~7 in the CF block)
findings.evidence: Read dash_devices.c:117-138 and 408-438. Callers: dashDevicesInit dash_main.c:1283, dashDevicesResetBaseline dash_main.c:362 (Grep). usb_rescan_next, the only extra field Reset clears, is a zero-initialised static at Init time.

findings.title: dash_files.c storage* wrappers branch on files_mode five times instead of choosing the screen once
findings.problem: storageEnter, storageInput, storageUpdate, storageDraw and storageHints each repeat 'if (dashCfg.files_mode) dashDevicesGridScreen.X(); else dashFilesListScreen.X();'.
findings.fix: Add one static function returning files_mode ? &dashDevicesGridScreen : &dashFilesListScreen and make each wrapper a one-line call through it.
findings.justification: One 4-line selector replaces five duplicated if/else pairs; net reduction of about 12 lines.
findings.evidence: Read dash_files.c:682-731. tests/test_zack_feedback.py:28-29 asserts 'dashCfg.files_mode = !dashCfg.files_mode' and the dashDevicesScreen initialiser, both kept.

findings.title: Dead bits in dash_editor.c: constant-empty status ternary, needless details[] buffer, avoidable forward declaration
findings.problem: editorScene formats '%s' with 'ndocs > 1 ? "" : ""', which is always empty. switchDocument snprintf's 'unsaved' or '' into a 128-byte details[8][16] stack array only to turn '' back into NULL. docNew is forward-declared because it is defined after its only earlier user docOpenPath.
findings.fix: Drop the trailing %s and its argument; set items[i].detail = docs[i].dirty ? "unsaved" : NULL and delete details[]; move docNew above docOpenPath and delete the forward declaration.
findings.evidence: Read dash_editor.c:410, 465-484, 718-734, 905-951. docNew callers: 438, 988, 1116 (all after its definition except 438).

findings.title: Hex Editor hexDigit duplicates dash_themes.c hexNibble and hexParse re-implements strtol
findings.problem: hexDigit (dash_editor.c:1221-1227) and hexNibble (dash_themes.c:646-655) are the same hex-digit decoder in two static copies; hexParse (1230-1242) hand-parses an optional 0x prefix and up to 7 hex digits, which strtol(s, &end, 16) already does (strtol is linked: dash_settings.c, ember_gameid.c).
findings.fix: Replace hexParse with strtol plus an end-pointer/empty check; keep one hex-digit helper (export one copy, or keep the editor's 7-line version and use it in dash_themes.c).
findings.benefit: ~12 lines (INFERRED: hexParse 13 -> ~4, one 7-10 line decoder dropped, +1 prototype)
findings.evidence: Grep 'static int (hex(Digit|Val|Nibble|Char)|from_hex|hexval)' -i over the repo: dash_editor.c:1221, dash_themes.c:646 (read both). hexParse only called at dash_editor.c:1469. Grep strtol\( in src: dash_settings.c, ember_gameid.c. tests/test_tile_styles.py:49 slices dash_themes.c starting at 'static int hexNibble', so keep that name if the theme copy stays.
